title: Required parameters in the builder's constructor, and a reusable builder

blocks.text: The page's `HttpRequest` puts the **required** values, the URL and the method, in the `Builder`'s **constructor**, so a builder without them can never exist; headers and a body are optional fluent steps. It also warns about **reusing a builder**: building twice from one builder must not let the second build's changes leak into the first request.

items: `new HttpRequest.Builder(url, method)` throws `NullPointerException` at once if either is `null`.
`build()` returns a request whose `headers()` is **a read-only map** that later builder calls never change; `body()` is `Optional.empty()` when unset.

cases.says: new Builder(url, method) with headers and a body builds a request that carries all of them.
new Builder(null, "GET") or new Builder(url, null) throws NullPointerException immediately, before any build().
A request built earlier from one builder is not changed by headers added to that builder later.
A request whose body was never set reports Optional.empty(), not an empty string.
Putting a header into a built request's headers() throws UnsupportedOperationException and leaves the request as it was.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Reusing one builder for several products shares its state unless each build() takes its own copy.
Required parameters go in the Builder's constructor and are checked there, while optional ones are set by fluent methods.
